title: Settings
sub: Nothing here changes your projects. Only physical arranging, once turned on, lets the app move files, and only when you ask.
folderAdded: Folder added: its projects come in at the next scan.
folderRemoved: Folder removed: its songs leave the app (nothing is touched on disk).
already: This folder is already in the list.

folders.sub: What the app reads. It only reads: your files stay as they are.
folders.projectsHint: The folders that hold your Ableton projects, subfolders included.
folders.samplesHint: Where to look for a sample a project can no longer find, on top of the projects folders and Ableton's library.
folders.midiHint: The MIDI files in your projects and samples folders are already read. Add other folders here (construction kits, packs): the app only reads the MIDI files in them.
folders.oldWindowsHint: An old Windows on another drive (dual boot): its plugins and samples help repair old projects.
folders.oldDriveSaved: Saved: used from the next scan.

arrange.sub: How the app arranges your songs.
arrange.physicalHint: Off, everything is arranged in the app only (releases, mood boards, folders): no file moves on your disk, Ctrl+Z included. On, you can also move and create folders, and put a release in its own folder. Every move is checked (a project that would lose a sample stays put) and can be undone with Ctrl+Z, after confirming.
arrange.physicalOn: On: the app can move files when you ask.
arrange.physicalOnSaid: Physical arranging on: files can be moved.
arrange.physicalOffSaid: Physical arranging off: nothing moves on disk any more.
arrange.artistsHint: One name per line. A song in a folder carrying one of these names belongs to that artist.
arrange.artistsSaved: Artists saved: the songs are arranged again.
arrange.wordsHint: Words you put in the name of a working copy ("test", "try"...): a file carrying them stays a version of the same song. One per line.
arrange.wordsSaved: Saved: the songs are arranged again.

data.sub: Scanning your projects, and what goes in or out of the app.
data.scanHint: The app rereads your projects as soon as they change, and at least every minute. "Reread everything" is only needed after an update of the app or of Live.
data.noLive: Live hasn't been opened on this computer yet: its plugin list is missing.
data.exportHint: Your songs in a CSV file for a spreadsheet (Excel, Google Sheets) or another tool: title, artist, style, key, tempo, stage, rating, catalogue, plugin status, reference render, dates, folder. You choose where to save it; nothing else is written.
data.notionHint: Export your Notion database as CSV (the database's ••• menu, Export, "Markdown & CSV"), then choose the file. You check which column goes where before anything is written, and Ctrl+Z undoes the import.
data.notionDialog: CSV export of the Notion database

spool.sub: The installed version and its updates.
spool.updatesHint: Spool checks for a newer version shortly after it starts, then every 6 hours. Nothing installs without your click, never during a scan or a repair, and only a version signed by Fatstep is accepted. Your database is copied before any update that changes it.

zero.hint: Empties the app's database: songs, stages, styles, notes, groupings, folders, artists, processing presets and repair history, then reopens the setup. Your projects, your samples and the copies already written are not touched. The old database is set aside (the last 2 are kept).
zero.confirm: Everything you arranged in the app will be removed. Continue?

fatstep.title: Publisher
fatstep.body: Spool is free and open source, made by Fatstep, a label and distributor for independent artists. When your songs are ready, we can help you release them.

theme.title: Appearance
theme.hint: Light or dark, or as Windows is set.

audio.title: Audio analysis
audio.hint: Listens to your reference renders to find the songs that sound alike, measure their tempo and suggest a style from the songs you have already sorted. Turning it on downloads about {mb} MB, once: the CLAP audio model (from Spool's page on GitHub) and Microsoft's ONNX Runtime (from Microsoft's page on GitHub), each file checked before use.
audio.privacy: The analysis runs on this computer only: nothing about your music is sent anywhere. Your renders are only read, never changed. It works in the background, one render at a time, and waits while a scan or a repair runs.
audio.credit: Model: CLAP larger_clap_general by LAION (laion.ai), Apache-2.0 licence. Runtime: ONNX Runtime by Microsoft, MIT licence.
audio.disable: Turn off (the analyses already made are kept)

paused.one: Paused. {n} reference render analysed out of {total}
paused.other: Paused. {n} reference renders analysed out of {total}

audio.kept: Turned off. The model is still on disk ({mb} MB).
audio.removeHint: Deletes the downloaded files to free the disk. What was already analysed stays.
audio.downloadStarted: Audio analysis on: downloading the model

storage.title: Storage
storage.hint: What Spool keeps on this computer, in its own folder. Your projects are not in it: they are neither counted nor touched here. Do not change anything in it by hand while Spool is open.
storage.midi: (of which {size} for the index of your MIDI files)
storage.backupsHint: Made before a Spool update that changes the format (the newest is kept 30 days), and when you start over (the two newest).
storage.trimConfirm: Delete the safety copies except the newest one? Your catalogue and your projects do not change.
storage.journal: (of which {size} of journal, emptied at the next start)
